subject.title: fix #95351: [Feature]: Generic JSONL line-parsing hook for CliBackendPlugin (native tool-card support beyond claude-stream-json)

question: Should OpenClaw publish `CliBackendPlugin.parseJsonlEvent` plus its normalized display-only tool-event union as a supported long-term plugin SDK contract?
rationale: The patch adds a new public extension API rather than repairing an established behavior; tests can validate mechanics but cannot decide the permanent plugin boundary and compatibility commitment.

options.title: Sponsor the public parser hook
options.body: Accept the backend-owned parser hook as the SDK boundary, then require end-to-end installed-plugin proof before merge.

options.title: Request a narrower API design
options.body: Keep the feature request open while owners specify a smaller or differently shaped stable plugin contract.

options.title: Decline the core SDK expansion
options.body: Close the implementation direction and retain the existing built-in JSONL dialect behavior until a broader plugin API need is established.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the public parser hook
recommendation.body: Accept the backend-owned parser hook as the SDK boundary, then require end-to-end installed-plugin proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work shows direct ownership of generalized CLI-backend behavior and its plugin contract.
